entities.summary: William of Saliceto (1210–1277) was an Italian surgeon and cleric in Saliceto. He was born in Saliceto, a small town in the province of Viterbo, Lazio, Italy, during the reign of Pope Innocent III. Saliceto was a major center of learning and medicine, attracting scholars and students from across Europe. William's contributions to surgery and medicine were significant, and he is considered one of the most important surgeons of the medieval period. He wrote several medical texts, including 'De medicina', which became a standard reference for surgeons for centuries. William's work had a lasting impact on the development of surgery and medicine, influencing generations of surgeons and physicians. His legacy can be seen in the many hospitals and medical schools that were established in his name, a testament to his enduring influence on the field of medicine. Through his contributions to surgery and medicine, William of Saliceto helped to advance the understanding of the human body and the treatment of diseases, saving countless lives and improving the quality of life for millions of people.
